title: Smallest Subarray to Sort in Every Sliding Window
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, for each contiguous subarray of length k, find the shortest segment that needs to be sorted to make the subarray non-decreasing.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, for each contiguous subarray of length k, find the shortest segment that needs to be sorted to make the subarray non-decreasing. Return an array of length n-k+1, where each element represents the required length for its respective subarray.
constraints: For each length-k window, sort one contiguous segment so the entire window becomes nondecreasing.
Return zero for windows already sorted.
reference_solution:
def sliding_window_sort_lengths(nums,k):
    answer=[]
    for start in range(len(nums)-k+1):
        end=start+k;maximum=-float('inf');right=-1
        for index in range(start,end):
            if nums[index]<maximum:right=index
            else:maximum=nums[index]
        if right<0:answer.append(0);continue
        minimum=float('inf');left=end
        for index in range(end-1,start-1,-1):
            if nums[index]>minimum:left=index
            else:minimum=nums[index]
        answer.append(right-left+1)
    return answer

hints: The required segment begins at the rightmost value exceeding a later minimum and ends at the left-to-right inversion frontier.
Within each window, scan forward for its last out-of-order index and backward for its first out-of-order index.
Track maximum from the left and minimum from the right; return right-left+1, or zero when no inversion exists.
Everything outside these two boundaries is already ordered relative to the window; sorting inside fixes every remaining inversion and no shorter segment can include both witnesses.
